question: Show me US large-cap stocks trading under 12x earnings right now. Just the outright cheap ones on a P/E basis.

_conventions._note: For the fields below, read the `definition` and/or `sign` before interpreting the value — a negative can MEAN something (an outflow, a benefit) and an ambiguous name needs its definition. Every other field is a plain magnitude.

eps_diluted.definition: PER SHARE, in the company's REPORTING currency (NOT USD-normalized like the _usd fields) — don't mix it with the USD amounts.

_pagination.note: Over-fetched ~4× your intended show (20) as a look-ahead buffer so 'a few more' is served from these 3 rows — do NOT re-screen for a few more. This is the COMPLETE match set — `count` is the exact total.

answer_to_user: Screening the US large-cap universe (126 names) for a trailing P/E below 12x, only three stocks come up outright cheap on earnings: AT&T (T.US) at ~8.2x, Progressive (PGR.US) at ~10.4x, and Capital One Financial (COF.US) at ~11.8x. That's the complete list — the vast majority of US large-caps trade above 12x right now, so genuine sub-12x names are scarce. All three also look reasonable on normalized (one-off-adjusted) P/E: AT&T ~7.7x, Progressive ~10.3x, Capital One ~12.1x. Two are financials (Progressive is insurance, Capital One a bank) where low multiples are common, and AT&T is a low-growth telecom — worth checking each isn't cheap for a structural reason.
